claim: DAMAKER integrates spatial and temporal data of cell populations, neuronal differentiation and brain morphogenesis, through in vivo imaging techniques paired with image analyses and segmentation tools.
source: DAMAKER integrates spatial and temporal data of cell populations, neuronal differentiation and brain morphogenesis, through in vivo imaging techniques paired with image analyses and segmentation tools.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the method developed in the study.

claim: The temporal order of neuronal differentiation prefigured the spatial distribution of neurons in the tissue, with an inner-outer differentiation gradient.
source: We generated digital neuronal birthdating 3D-maps and revealed that the temporal order of neuronal differentiation prefigured the spatial distribution of neurons in the tissue, with an inner-outer differentiation gradient.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pioneer work in Drosophila provided 3D-registration atlases and software that can automatically find the corresponding landmarks in a subject brain, and map them to the coordinate system of a target brain.
source: Pioneer work in Drosophila provided 3D-registration atlases and software that can automatically find the corresponding landmarks in a subject brain, and map them to the coordinate system of a target brain (Heckscher et al., 2014; Peng et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The incorporation of time in 3D-atlases is still one of the main challenges that needs to be solved.
source: However, up to now, the incorporation of time —and therefore information of tissue morphogenesis— in 3D-atlases is still one of the main challenges that needs to be solved.
evidence: This is stated as a current limitation in the field based on the authors' assessment of existing literature.

claim: Existing gene expression 3D-atlases in larval and adult fish provide valuable tools.
source: Existing gene expression 3D-atlases in larval and adult fish provide valuable tools (Chow et al., 2020; Jaggard et al., 2020; Kenney et al., 2021; Kunst et al., 2019; Ronneberger et al., 2012; Tabor et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to existing work.

claim: Whole brain images are particularly hard to register across space and time.
source: However, to incorporate the temporal component has been challenging, most probably because whole brain images are particularly hard to register across space and time, even though there are recent efforts aiming to make this more accessible (Dsilva et al., 2015; Fernandez and Moisy, 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The hindbrain is the most conserved vertebrate brain vesicle.
source: We made use of the hindbrain, which is the most conserved vertebrate brain vesicle (Murakami et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The hindbrain undergoes tissue segmentation along the anteroposterior (AP) axis leading to the formation of seven rhombomeres.
source: We made use of the hindbrain, which is the most conserved vertebrate brain vesicle (Murakami et al., 2005) and undergoes tissue segmentation along the anteroposterior (AP) axis leading to the formation of seven rhombomeres (Fraser et al., 1990; Jimenez-Guri et al., 2010; Kiecker and Lumsden, 2005; Krumlauf and Wilkinson, 2021; Pujades, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Initial neuronal differentiation in the hindbrain starts prior to 24 hours post-fertilization (hpf) with a pronounced increase from 30hpf onwards.
source: This morphogenetic process is accompanied with the initial neuronal differentiation, which starts prior 24hours post-fertilization (hpf) with a pronounced increase from 30hpf onwards (Voltes et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Neuronal differentiation involves changes in cell proliferative capacity and an extraordinary displacement of neurons from their birth site.
source: Neuronal differentiation involves changes in cell proliferative capacity and an extraordinary displacement of neurons from their birth site, and occurs while other dramatic changes take place, such as the generation of the brain ventricle (Belzunce et al., 2020; Gutzman et al., 2008; Hevia et al., 2022; Lyons et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Previous work evoked the importance of the temporal order of neuronal differentiation in ascribing final neuronal position within specific circuits.
source: Although previous work evoked the importance of the temporal order of neuronal differentiation in ascribing final neuronal position within specific circuits (Kinkhabwala et al., 2011; Pujala and Koyama, 2019; Wan et al., 2019), little is known about its impact in the final organization of differentiated neurons within the hindbrain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Little is known about the impact of temporal order of neuronal differentiation in the final organization of differentiated neurons within the hindbrain.
source: Although previous work evoked the importance of the temporal order of neuronal differentiation in ascribing final neuronal position within specific circuits (Kinkhabwala et al., 2011; Pujala and Koyama, 2019; Wan et al., 2019), little is known about its impact in the final organization of differentiated neurons within the hindbrain.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: DAMAKER uses Fijiyama registration tool which allows multi-modal rigid registration.
source: The expandable zebrafish digital 3D-atlas was created by combining in vivo imaging data from distinct transgenic embryos with the Fijiyama registration tool (Fernandez and Moisy, 2020), which allows multi-modal rigid registration
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by a citation.

claim: DAMAKER uses Trainable Weka Segmentation (TWS) that leverages a limited number of manual annotations and permits data to be automatically segmented after a short training.
source: The expandable zebrafish digital 3D-atlas was created by combining in vivo imaging data from distinct transgenic embryos with the Fijiyama registration tool (Fernandez and Moisy, 2020), which allows multi-modal rigid registration, and the Trainable Weka Segmentation (TWS) (Arganda-Carreras et al., 2017) that leverages a limited number of manual annotations and permits data to be automatically segmented after a short training and to quantify tissue volumes.
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by a citation.

claim: Early-born neurons were always located in the inner part of the differentiation domain and surrounded by younger neurons, generating an inner-outer gradient of older vs. younger neurons.
source: By generating these maps, we unveiled that early-born neurons were always located in the inner part of the differentiation domain and surrounded by younger neurons, generating an inner–outer gradient of older vs. younger neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: The digital 3D-atlas maker (DAMAKER) is a dynamic and expandable 3D-tool for monitoring the temporal changes in growth and shape during tissue morphogenesis.
source: Here, we developed a digital 3D-atlas maker (DAMAKER), which is a dynamic and expandable 3D-tool for monitoring the temporal changes in growth and shape during tissue morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a description of the tool developed in the study.

claim: DAMAKER uses open-access tools and algorithms.
source: Our goal is to share an established protocol using open-access tools and algorithms that allow standardized and accessible tissue-wide cell population atlas construction and can be used to create an expandable atlas of any tissue in any organism.
evidence: This is stated as a feature of the developed method.

claim: DAMAKER can be used to create an expandable atlas of any tissue in any organism.
source: Our goal is to share an established protocol using open-access tools and algorithms that allow standardized and accessible tissue-wide cell population atlas construction and can be used to create an expandable atlas of any tissue in any organism.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the method.

claim: Fijiyama plugin in FIJI allowed a multi-modal automatic rigid registration process and a large range of customization.
source: To improve comparison of various signals across embryos that requires an alignment/registration, which is often done manually and is very time-consuming, we used the Fijiyama plugin in FIJI (Schindelin et al., 2012). This allowed a multi-modal automatic rigid registration process and a large range of customization
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by a citation.

claim: Fijiyama permitted the application of a previously computed transform to another channel that shares no features with the reference signal.
source: This allowed a multi-modal automatic rigid registration process and a large range of customization, and it permitted the application of a previously computed transform; namely, an alignment can be computed using one channel of an embryo matching the chosen reference and this can be applied to another channel that shares no features with the reference signal.
evidence: This is a methodological description of the tool's capabilities.

claim: Trainable Weka Segmentation 3D (TWS) combines the image processing toolkit FIJI with machine learning algorithms provided in WEKA.
source: To overcome this problem, we used the Trainable Weka Segmentation 3D (TWS), (Arganda-Carreras et al., 2017), which combines the image processing toolkit FIJI with the state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms provided in the latest version of the data mining and machine learning toolkit Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis (WEKA) (Hall et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by citations.

claim: TWS is modular, allows sophisticated data mining processes to be built, is open-sourced, and can be easily used as a plugin of FIJI.
source: This tool is modular, allows sophisticated data mining processes to be built from the wide collection of base learning algorithms and tools provided, is open-sourced, and can be easily used as a plugin of FIJI.
evidence: This is a description of the tool's features.

claim: Most of the currently used approaches for cell birthdating either lack whole population coverage or are limited by expression timing of the gene or transgene.
source: Until now, most of the currently used approaches either lack whole population coverage or are limited by expression timing of the gene or transgene
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods.

claim: The combination of photoconversion experiments and DAMAKER provides neuronal birthdating 3D-maps.
source: Here, with the combination of photoconversion experiments as a tool to register temporality of neuronal differentiation and DAMAKER, we provide neuronal birthdating 3D-maps
evidence: This is a description of the method and its output.

claim: The order of neuronal differentiation prefigured the spatial distribution of neurons in the hindbrain, with an inner-outer gradient of temporal differentiation.
source: Here, with the combination of photoconversion experiments as a tool to register temporality of neuronal differentiation and DAMAKER, we provide neuronal birthdating 3D-maps and revealed that the order of neuronal differentiation prefigured the spatial distribution of neurons in the hindbrain, with an inner-outer gradient of temporal differentiation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Most of the available transgenic lines were generated with random insertion systems that do not always recapitulate the right onset of gene expression.
source: Usually, expression of the reporter genes in transgenic lines is delayed as compared to the gene expression onset, unless the reporter has been inserted within the given gene locus. Now, we can specifically knock-in genes within a targeted genome site thanks to the CRISPR-Cas technology, but most of the available —and very valuable—transgenic lines were (and still are) generated with random insertion systems that do not always recapitulate the right onset of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of transgenic lines.

claim: The digital 3D-atlas can be used for predicting neuronal birthdates by analyzing the position of neurons in the differentiation domain.
source: Thus, our tool can be very useful for predicting neuronal birthdates just by analyzing the position of neurons in the differentiation domain as we showed with glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated application of the tool.

claim: The developed digital platform will be useful to interrogate phenotypes in neurological diseases.
source: Besides that, this developed digital platform will be useful to interrogate phenotypes in neurological diseases, and zebrafish avatars from human neurological disorders could be analyzed in a very simple manner.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the tool.

claim: Tissue shape comparisons were performed after modulating neurogenesis using pharmacological treatments as a proof-of-concept.
source: As a proof-of-concept, we show tissue shape comparisons after modulating neurogenesis using pharmacological treatments.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental demonstration.

claim: DAMAKER can be further improved by using batch processing algorithms.
source: In the future, DAMAKER can be further improved by using batch processing algorithms (e.g., to assess the effects of pharmacological treatments or gene disruptions)
evidence: This is stated as a potential future improvement.

claim: DAMAKER can be adjusted for more geometrically complex tissues or for tissues with less alignment features.
source: In the future, DAMAKER can be further improved by using batch processing algorithms (e.g., to assess the effects of pharmacological treatments or gene disruptions) or by adjusting for more geometrically complex tissues or for tissues with less alignment features (such as heart).
evidence: This is stated as a potential future application.

claim: DAMAKER pipeline could be applied to time-lapse videos by repeating the process for each frame.
source: Last but not least, this pipeline could be applied to time-lapse videos by repeating the process for each frame.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application.

claim: Tg[HuC:GFP] embryos at 72hpf display GFP uniformly in the whole neuronal differentiation domain.
source: Since we were interested in neuronal differentiation patterns, to establish a reference tissue signal we made use of Tg[HuC:GFP] embryos at 72hpf, a stage in which most of the cells have undergone neuronal differentiation and GFP is uniformly displayed in the whole neuronal differentiation domain (Hevia et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the transgenic line used, supported by a citation.

claim: Rigid registration was favored in the Fijiyama registration process, although non-rigid registration could be considered at the cost of sample shape variability.
source: Acquired 3D-images from different Tg[HuC:GFP] embryos (e1–eY; n=5each) were registered to the reference by Fijiyama registration, in which rigid registration was favored, although non-rigid registration could be considered at the cost of sample shape variability.
evidence: This is a methodological choice explained in the text.

claim: Segmentation settings were at tissue scale to keep computing power low for pipeline accessibility.
source: After alignment of 3D-images, tissue segmentation was applied in order to generate binary masks for each labeling/staining (Figure 1B). Here, segmentation settings were at tissue scale, both in an effort to keep computing power low for pipeline accessibility and for our interest in cell populations, although single cell resolution could be achieved with nuclear reporter lines.
evidence: This is a methodological choice explained in the text.

claim: Single cell resolution could be achieved with nuclear reporter lines.
source: Here, segmentation settings were at tissue scale, both in an effort to keep computing power low for pipeline accessibility and for our interest in cell populations, although single cell resolution could be achieved with nuclear reporter lines.
evidence: This is stated as a potential capability of the method.

claim: Different users were invited to employ the Trainable Weka Segmentation (TWS) tool to train classifiers to reduce the potential impact of human bias.
source: In order to discern noise vs. signal in the raw data from each embryo, different users (u1–uX; n=5) were invited to employ the Trainable Weka Segmentation (TWS) tool to train classifiers (one per user) (Figure 1B). In the case of low or sparse signals (or specific structures within a signal) specific training of the algorithm with different settings would be better to leverage the structural recognition capabilities of TWS. To reduce the potential impact of the human bias from the trained classifiers, we averaged the resulting segmented images from multiple users' trained classifiers (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a methodological approach to reduce bias.

claim: Signal consensus among at least 3 embryos was used for the generation of the models.
source: Signal consensus among 3 or more embryos was used for the generation of the models.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological threshold in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The interindividual variability between the HuC volume of the individuals and the HuC volume of the generated 3D-model never exceeded 10%.
source: Note that this difference never exceeded 10%.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and shown in the corresponding figure.

claim: Tg[Mu4127;HuC:GFP] embryos display DsRed in r3 and r5.
source: Thus, we imaged Tg[Mu4127;HuC:GFP] embryos, which displayed DsRed in r3 and r5 (Distel et al., 2009), and GFP in the neuronal differentiation domain (Figure 2A–A').
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the transgenic line, supported by a citation.

claim: The Mu4127 signal distribution was concentrated in r3 and r5 along the anteroposterior (AP) axis.
source: Accordingly, the signal distribution was concentrated in r3 and r5 along the anteroposterior (AP) axis, whereas it was similarly distributed along the mediolateral (ML) axis (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Mu4127 signal was similarly distributed along the mediolateral (ML) axis.
source: Accordingly, the signal distribution was concentrated in r3 and r5 along the anteroposterior (AP) axis, whereas it was similarly distributed along the mediolateral (ML) axis (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Tg[neurog1:DsRed;HuC:GFP] embryos show a striped-pattern distribution of neurog1-derivatives in the neuronal differentiated domain.
source: In Tg[neurog1:DsRed;HuC:GFP] embryos, we observed the striped-pattern distribution of neurog1-derivatives in the neuronal differentiated domain (Figure 2C–C'; Figure 2—video 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C-C'.

claim: The automatic quantification of the neurog1-volume displayed differences in the ratio of labeling along the AP axis.
source: The automatic quantification of the neurog1-volume displayed differences in the ratio of labeling along the AP axis (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Neuronal differentiated regions have less neurog1-derivatives when compared with more posterior domains.
source: The automatic quantification of the neurog1-volume displayed differences in the ratio of labeling along the AP axis (Figure 2D), supporting the observation of neuronal differentiated regions with less neurog1-derivatives when compared with more posterior domains (Figure 2C–C', see white asterisk in the lateral r5).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C-C'.

claim: neurog1-derivatives display a more medial distribution in the hindbrain when compared with the spinal cord.
source: In addition, the more medial distribution of neurog1-derivatives in the hindbrain was observed (Figure 2D) when compared with the spinal cord as it was previously described (Belzunce et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the text, shown in Figure 2D, and supported by a citation.

claim: Motoneurons display a ventral and medial position in the hindbrain.
source: For mapping distinct neuronal differentiation programs, we first analyzed the spatial distribution of motoneurons by using Tg[isl1:GFP;HuC:KaedeRed] embryos and observed their ventral and medial position (Figure 2E–E'; Figure 2—video 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2E-E'.

claim: Motoneurons show higher signal in discrete patterns along the AP axis with a clear increase in the spinal cord.
source: Upon quantification, higher signal was observed in discrete patterns along the AP axis with a clear increase in the spinal cord (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Glutamatergic neurons contribute mainly to the most dorsolateral neuronal differentiation domain.
source: Using Tg[vglut2a:DsRed;HuC:GFP] and Tg[gad1b:DsRed;HuC:GFP] embryos we observed the main contribution of glutamatergic neurons to the most dorsolateral neuronal differentiation domain (Figure 2G–G')
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2G-G'.

claim: GABAergic neurons allocate more medially in the hindbrain.
source: Using Tg[vglut2a:DsRed;HuC:GFP] and Tg[gad1b:DsRed;HuC:GFP] embryos we observed the main contribution of glutamatergic neurons to the most dorsolateral neuronal differentiation domain (Figure 2G–G'), whereas GABAergic neurons allocated more medially (Figure 2I–I').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2I-I'.

claim: Glutamatergic neurons show a smaller contribution to the r3-r5 region at 72hpf.
source: We observed a smaller contribution of glutamatergic neurons to the r3-r5 region (Figure 2H)
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2H.

claim: GABAergic signal at 72hpf is enriched in r2 when compared to the rest of the hindbrain.
source: whereas GABAergic signal at this stage was enriched in r2 (Figure 2J) when compared to the rest of the hindbrain.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The quantification of neurotransmitter expression recapitulated the spatially restricted domains previously described.
source: This quantification recapitulated the spatially restricted domains of neurotransmitter expression (Figure 2G' and I') previously described (Kinkhabwala et al., 2011; Koyama et al., 2011; Pujala and Koyama, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text, shown in figures, and supported by citations.

claim: The stripe patterning of alx-expressing neurons, which are involved in swimming behavior, is age-related.
source: The stripe patterning of alx-expressing neurons, which are involved in swimming behavior, is age-related (Kinkhabwala et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The position of the V2a cell body and the order of spinal projections in the hindbrain relies on their neuronal birth.
source: and the position of the V2a cell body and the order of spinal projections in the hindbrain relies on their neuronal birth (Pujala and Koyama, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The onset of neuronal differentiation was before 24hpf.
source: We observed that the onset of neuronal differentiation was before 24hpf and that the first differentiated neurons located more ventral and medial than late-born cells (Figure 3A–A'; see magenta vs. green cells in 3 A').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A-A'.

claim: The first differentiated neurons located more ventral and medial than late-born cells.
source: We observed that the onset of neuronal differentiation was before 24hpf and that the first differentiated neurons located more ventral and medial than late-born cells (Figure 3A–A'; see magenta vs. green cells in 3 A').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A-A'.

claim: Neuronal differentiation dramatically increased between 24hpf and 36hpf.
source: When we labeled the neurons born before 36hpf we appreciated that neuronal differentiation dramatically increased between 24hpf and 36hpf, since the magenta territory in this case was larger
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B-B'.

claim: Later differentiated neurons piled up on the top of the previously differentiated ones.
source: When we labeled the neurons born before 36hpf we appreciated that neuronal differentiation dramatically increased between 24hpf and 36hpf, since the magenta territory in this case was larger, and that later differentiated neurons piled up on the top of the previously differentiated ones (Figure 3B–B'; see magenta vs. green cells in 3B').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B-B'.

claim: Neurons born at different stages were precisely organized at 48hpf.
source: We overlapped and color-coded them according to the neuronal birthdate, and observed that neurons born at different stages were precisely organized at 48hpf (Figure 3C—C'; see youngest neurons in blue, neurons differentiated between 24 and 36hpf in green, and the oldest ones in magenta).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C-C'.

claim: Many neurons differentiated between 24 and 36hpf.
source: Many neurons differentiated between 24 and 36hpf (compare Figure 3A' and B'), and they surrounded the existing differentiated neurons generating an inner-outer differentiation gradient (Figure 3C').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Neurons differentiated between 24 and 36hpf surrounded the existing differentiated neurons generating an inner-outer differentiation gradient.
source: Many neurons differentiated between 24 and 36hpf (compare Figure 3A' and B'), and they surrounded the existing differentiated neurons generating an inner-outer differentiation gradient (Figure 3C').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C'.

claim: EdU-cells are exclusively in the newly differentiated domain, stacking dorsally, with no signal indicating a migration of newly born neurons in the older neuronal domain.
source: We observed cells with EdU-incorporation exclusively in the newly differentiated domain, stacking dorsally, with no signal indicating a migration of newly born neurons in the older neuronal domain, therefore confirming the establishment of segregated domains according to neuronal differentiation timings (Figure 3E—E').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3E-E'.

claim: Early differentiated neurons at 72hpf were located more ventrally and medially, and late-born cells piled up.
source: As before, we observed that early differentiated neurons were located more ventrally and medially, and that late-born cells piled up (Figure 3F–H, 3F'–H'; see magenta vs. green cells in 3F'–H').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3F-H.

claim: The differentiation capacity diminished with time.
source: To monitor possible differences in the spatiotemporal distribution within the neuronal differentiation domain, we generated the neuronal birthdate 3D-map at 72hpf and observed that the differentiation capacity diminished with time (Figure 3I–I''; see small yellow domain).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3I-I''.

claim: By 48hpf, almost the whole differentiation domain was already occupied by previously differentiated neurons.
source: Indeed, by 48hpf, almost the whole differentiation domain was already occupied by previously differentiated neurons (Figure 3I–I''; see blue, green and magenta domains).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3I-I''.

claim: The overall HuC-volumes did not dramatically change among embryos that underwent HuC:KaedeGreen photoconversion at different stages.
source: For this, we first checked that the overall HuC-volumes did not dramatically change among embryos that underwent HuC:KaedeGreen photoconversion at different stages (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, C.

claim: Average individuals' variability from the HuC volume model did not exceed 15%.
source: Second, we calculated the difference between the HuC volume of the individuals and the generated models and showed that average individuals' variability from the model did not exceed 15% (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: HuC:KaedeRed cells labeled in an early conversion were included in the HuC:KaedeRed domain labeled in a late conversion.
source: Next, we verified that the HuC:KaedeRed cells labeled in an early conversion were included in the HuC:KaedeRed domain labeled in a late conversion. For this, we overlaid the differentiation domains contributed at each time interval (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–J,H'–J').
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H-J.

claim: At 48hpf, of the whole differentiated domain (12.07 [SD ± 1.36]×10^6 μm^3), only a small part comprised neurons differentiated before 24hpf (3.42 [SD ± 1.56]×10^6 μm^3 early-born neurons vs. 8.64 [SD ± 0.86]×10^6 μm^3 late-born neurons).
source: We detected that at 48hpf, of the whole differentiated domain (12.07 [SD ± 1.36]×106 μm3), only a small part comprised neurons differentiated before 24hpf (3.42 [SD ± 1.56]×106 μm3 early-born neurons vs. 8.64 [SD ± 0.86]×106 μm3 late-born neurons)
evidence: This is a quantitative result stated in the text.

claim: Most of the differentiated neurons at 48hpf arose before 36hpf (9.61 [SD ± 0.68]×10^6 μm^3) and the rest differentiated between 36 and 48hpf (3.10 [SD ± 0.35]×10^6 μm^3).
source: whereas most of the differentiated neurons arose before 36hpf (9.61 [SD ± 0.68]×106 μm3) and the rest differentiated between 36 and 48hpf (3.10 [SD ± 0.35]×106 μm3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result stated in the text.

claim: Neurons born at 24hpf located more ventrally than neurons born at 36hpf.
source: When quantifying the signal ratio along the axes, we could observe similar dynamics along the AP and ML axes between 24hpf and 36hpf, and a clear difference along the DV demonstrating that neurons born at 24hpf located more ventrally than neurons born at 36hpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: At 72hpf, only a small part of the differentiation domain came from neurons born before 24hpf (2.77 [SD ± 1.23]×10^6 μm^3 for early-born vs. 11.88 [SD ± 1.28]×10^6 μm^3 for late-born).
source: When volumes were quantified at 72hpf, we observed that only a small part of the differentiation domain came from neurons born before 24hpf (2.77 [SD ± 1.23]×106 μm3 for early-born vs. 11.88 [SD ± 1.28]×106 μm3 for late-born).
evidence: This is a quantitative result stated in the text.

claim: Most neurons at 72hpf underwent differentiation between 24hpf and 48hpf, with half of the differentiated neurons arising before 36hpf (6.75 [SD ± 2.19]×10^6 μm^3 born before 36hpf vs. 7.58 [SD ± 2.37]×10^6 μm^3 after 36hpf).
source: Most neurons underwent differentiation between 24hpf and 48hpf, with half of the differentiated neurons arising before 36hpf (6.75 [SD ± 2.19]×106 μm3 born before 36hpf vs. 7.58 [SD ± 2.37]×106 μm3 after 36hpf)
evidence: This is a quantitative result stated in the text.

claim: At 72hpf, the rest of neurons were differentiated between 36 and 48hpf (11.19 [SD ± 1.09]×10^6 μm^3 born before 48hpf vs. 2.99 [SD ± 0.90]×10^6 μm^3 after 48hpf).
source: and the rest were differentiated between 36 and 48hpf (11.19 [SD ± 1.09]×106 μm3 born before 48hpf vs. 2.99 [SD ± 0.90]×106 μm3 after 48hpf).
evidence: This is a quantitative result stated in the text.

claim: A steady increase of neuronal differentiation domain was observed at 72hpf (24hpf: 0.21 ± 0.04; 36hpf: 0.47 ± 0.16; 48hpf: 0.79 ± 0.07).
source: When the ratio of neurons born at different stages over the whole neuronal differentiation domain was assessed, a steady increase of neuronal differentiation domain was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C; 24hpf: 0.21 ± 0.04; 36hpf: 0.47 ± 0.16; 48hpf: 0.79 ± 0.07).
evidence: This is a quantitative result stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Early-born neurons (24-36hpf) display a more ventral enrichment along the DV axis at 72hpf.
source: As expected, when the analysis was performed along the DV axis, differences in cell allocation relying on the neuronal birthdate could be appreciated, with early-born neurons (24-36hpf) displaying a more ventral enrichment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, see DV-axis graph).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Most of the neuronal differentiation events occurred between 24 and 48hpf.
source: Overall, the overlaying of birthdating 3D-maps showed that most of the neuronal differentiation events occurred between 24 and 48hpf
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data.

claim: Glutamatergic neurons contributed in a big proportion to the differentiation domain and were born during all the analyzed temporal windows.
source: Glutamatergic neurons contributed in a big proportion to the differentiation domain, and were born during all the analyzed temporal windows (Figure 4—video 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—video 1A-B.

claim: Glutamatergic neurons displayed the inner-outer distribution depending on birth-time, with the oldest cells in the inner domain.
source: They displayed the inner-outer distribution depending on birth-time, with the oldest cells cells in the inner domain (see magenta cells in Figure 4A'–B'; Figure 4—video 1A–B), and the youngest neurons in the most outer position (see blue and yellow domains in Figure 4A'–B'; Figure 4—video 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A'-B'.

claim: Some GABAergic neurons in r3 and r5 were born as early as 24 hpf.

Some GABAergic neurons in r3 and r5 were born as early as 24 hpf (Figure 4C–C'; Figure 4—video 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C-C'.

claim: An important part of glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons was born between 24 and 36hpf, although some were born earlier and later too.
source: These observations suggested that an important part of glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons was born between 24 and 36hpf, although some were born earlier and later too.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: Of the total glutamatergic neurons, approximately 20% were contributed by cells born before 24hpf, 60% by cells born between 26 and 36hpf, and only a small percentage by neurons born between 36 and 48hpf.
source: Accordingly, when assessing the relative contribution of neurons born at different intervals to the corresponding neuronal populations, we observed that of the total glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, approximately 20% and 30%, respectively, were contributed by cells born before 24hpf, 60% by cells born between 26 and 36hpf, and only by a small percentage of neurons born between 36 and 48hpf (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E-F.

claim: Of the total GABAergic neurons, approximately 30% were contributed by cells born before 24hpf, 60% by cells born between 26 and 36hpf, and only a small percentage by neurons born between 36 and 48hpf.
source: Accordingly, when assessing the relative contribution of neurons born at different intervals to the corresponding neuronal populations, we observed that of the total glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, approximately 20% and 30%, respectively, were contributed by cells born before 24hpf, 60% by cells born between 26 and 36hpf, and only by a small percentage of neurons born between 36 and 48hpf (Figure 4E–F).

claim: Glutamatergic neurons were produced earlier than GABAergic neurons at 72hpf.
source: Comparison of the growth dynamics of both populations at 72hpf showed that they were slightly different, with glutamatergic neurons produced earlier than GABAergic neurons (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Position of differentiated neurons at 72hpf could recapitulate neuronal birthdates.
source: Overall, this analysis indicated that position of differentiated neurons at 72hpf could recapitulate neuronal birthdates.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons were already specified at 24hpf and they were located within the HuC territory.
source: Indeed, glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons were already specified at 24hpf and they were located within the HuC territory (Figure 4H–H'')

claim: The neuronal birthdating 3D-map can be used as a proxy to infer neuronal differentiation order.
source: Thus, these results demonstrate that the neuronal birthdating 3D-map can be used as a proxy to infer neuronal differentiation order, and widens the use of the digital 3D-atlas.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: The glutamatergic populations born between 24 and 36hpf and between 36 and 48hpf underwent a drastic displacement along the dorsoventral (DV) axis when comparing 48hpf to 72hpf.

claim: The 24-36hpf glutamatergic neuronal subset, which displayed a relatively homogenous distribution along the DV axis when observed at 48hpf, was medially located at 72hpf.

claim: The 36-48hpf glutamatergic subset, mostly dorsal when observed at 48hpf, was distributed both ventrally and dorsally when observed at 72hpf.

claim: Newly produced neurons initially located dorsally were displaced towards ventral, resulting in the formation of the inner to outer gradient of neuronal differentiation.

evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: The 48-72hpf subset of glutamatergic neurons is more laterally located than the GABAergic 48-72hpf subset, which was enriched medially.
source: In addition, the medio-lateral distribution of the neurons produced at different time intervals recapitulated the different allocations of late born glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, with the 48-72hpf subset of glutamatergic neurons more laterally located than the GABAergic 48-72hpf subset, which was enriched medially (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: Notch-pathway plays an important role during hindbrain neurogenesis.
source: For this, we disturbed embryonic neurogenesis by conditionally inhibiting the Notch-pathway, which has been demonstrated to play an important role during hindbrain neurogenesis (Hevia et al., 2022; Nikolaou et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: When Notch-signaling was downregulated, there was an increase in newly differentiated neurons that dramatically impacted the early-born neuronal domain.
source: When comparing control embryos with those in which Notch-signaling was downregulated, we observed an increase in newly differentiated neurons that dramatically impacted in the early-born neuronal domain, since newer neurons occupied the most dorsal part of the hindbrain displacing the older neurons (Figure 5B–B' and C–C') as previously described (Belzunce et al., 2020; Hevia et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the text, shown in Figure 5B-C', and supported by citations.

claim: Upon Notch-signaling inhibition, newer neurons occupied the most dorsal part of the hindbrain displacing the older neurons.
source: When comparing control embryos with those in which Notch-signaling was downregulated, we observed an increase in newly differentiated neurons that dramatically impacted in the early-born neuronal domain, since newer neurons occupied the most dorsal part of the hindbrain displacing the older neurons (Figure 5B–B' and C–C') as previously described (Belzunce et al., 2020; Hevia et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the text, shown in Figure 5B-C', and supported by citations.

evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5F-F'.

claim: The brain ventricle was distorted due to the increase of neurons upon Notch-inhibition.
source: This result was supported by the previous observation in which the brain ventricle was distorted due to the increase of neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a supporting observation.

source: The increased differentiated domain volume was visible mainly in the dorsomedial part, which was occupied by new neurons and remodeled the neuronal differentiation domain.
